ideal: It must be possible for a list to have more than three clauses, all beginning with the same subject.
note: fused two list-wide conditions into one description

ideal: When a list is a rule whose two sides are each one clause, and neither side begins with a time phrase, verbalizer says the list without "then".
note: combined the two 'not TimeFirst'/'not TimeSecond' bullets into 'neither side'

ideal: When the formula of a unit cannot be said in words, checker says why.

For every scenario and every unit: when the scenario cannot happen while every held unit holds, the analyzer is asked to hold the formula of the unit, and the author has not asked about leaving out any unit for the scenario, then some search that leaves out only this unit requires the scenario to happen.
note: turned the no-unit existential into 'has not asked about leaving out any unit'

ideal:
All of these hold:
- Now and at every later moment, for every owner_1, owner_2, and cleanup: when pulse disposes owner_1, owner_1 is the parent of owner_2, pulse has not disposed owner_2, code has registered the cleanup, the cleanup has not run, and the cleanup is on owner_1, then the cleanup does not run until pulse disposes owner_2.
- Now and at every later moment, for every owner_3, owner_4, and owner_5: when pulse disposes owner_3, owner_3 is the parent of owner_4 and of owner_5, owner_4 was created before owner_5, and pulse has not disposed owner_4 or owner_5, then pulse does not dispose owner_4 until it disposes owner_5.
note: replaced the 'now-or-later' plus 'until-not-including' bullet pairs with plain 'until', which means exactly that

ideal: When a quantifier has no fact for its variable beside another thing, verbalizer says it in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.

For every run, command, and unit: when the run asks for the `generate` or `check` command and the verbalizer fails on the formula of the unit with a fault of its own, then checker does not say why the formula of the unit cannot be said, and the run does not exit with code 0.
note: folded the command variable's identity into 'asks for the generate or check command'

ideal: When a unit holds a formula that can be said in words, its statement sits between the markers of a generated region, and that statement differs from what the formula says, then the statement is stale.
It must be possible for a quantifier's variable to be the subject of the sentence while its reading says the variable twice.
When a list is a rule with a first side and a second, but not one whose two sides are each one clause, verbalizer puts "then" at the start of the second side, on a line of its own.
When a list is a rule whose two sides are each one clause, and its first side does not begin with a time phrase, verbalizer says it on one line, as "when" the first side, the second side.
When a definition has an alternative that says something about another unit, verbalizer says it as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
It must be possible for a list to have three clauses or fewer and still be longer than a line when put in a sentence.
note: added 'still' to carry the conjunction naturally

ideal: For every two documents and every unit: when the project checks the first document but not the second, the second is context for the first, and the second holds the unit, then checker does not write the statement of the unit when it generates.
It must be possible for a scenario that cannot happen while every held unit holds to be reported by checker as impossible, with a unit named in that report whose removal lets the scenario happen.
note: merged the four flat conjuncts around the report naming the freeing unit

ideal: When a list has an item that is more than one clause, verbalizer says it as bullets.
For every two different units and every word: when a block of the second unit names the word outside its declaration, checker does not report the formula of the first unit as lone on that word.

When a definition's alternatives each begin with the kind of the subject, and it can be said kind by kind, verbalizer says it as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom".
For every run, check command, unit, and word: when the run asks for the check command and checker reports the formula of the unit as lone on the word, the run does not exit with code 0.
When a definition has two alternatives for one kind and can be said kind by kind, verbalizer says it as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or.
When a unit's statement is current, checker does not report it.

Now and at every later moment: when code disposes an owner that pulse has already disposed, that call does not run any cleanup that is registered on the owner and has not run, and that call does not throw.
note: fused the two 'always no' conjuncts, which share the same situation, into one when/then sentence

ideal: When a scenario cannot happen while every held unit holds, checker reports that it cannot happen.

It must be possible that there are owner_1, owner_2, and failing_cleanup_1 such that owner_2 is the nearest error handler or boundary above owner_1, and pulse eventually disposes owner_1 while failing_cleanup_1 is on it; then failing_cleanup_1 eventually runs; and then its error eventually reaches owner_2.
note: used a 'then eventually' chain to keep the nested-eventually order without separate bullets

ideal: When a unit holds more than one formula, the formula of the unit cannot be said in words.
When a list has more than three clauses, verbalizer says it as bullets.
When a list is longer than a line once put in a sentence, verbalizer says it as bullets.
When a definition has a run of and beside another alternative of its kind, verbalizer says it as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
When the formula of a unit cannot be said in words, checker does not write its statement when it generates.

A quantifier fits a noun phrase exactly when none of these hold: its reading says the variable twice; it has no fact for its variable beside another thing; it says no variable differs from another and holds a condition; its condition is not about its variable; or it has several conditions, one of which begins with a time phrase.
note: turned five 'is not' bullets into one 'none of these hold' list

ideal: It must be possible for a document to extend a second document that extends a third, different from the first, with the third being context for the first.
note: chained the extend relations instead of listing them flat

ideal: It must be possible for a run to call an installed plugin that checker runs over a document whose frontmatter lists that plugin, get code 1 back from it, and itself exit with code 1.
note: fused the frontmatter/listing pair into one relative clause

ideal: When a unit holds a formula, is not a term, and no other formula can contradict its formula, then checker reports its formula as lone on some signature.
note: pronoun for repeated 'formula of the unit'

ideal: When checker reports that a scenario cannot happen, and leaving out a unit would let it happen, checker names that unit in its report of the scenario.
When a unit's statement is current, checker does not write it when it generates.
When some unit's reading says a word, and no unit declares it, then it is a word that a reading says and nothing declares.
note: folded the existential into 'some unit's reading says'

ideal: When an exception cites no fact, checker reports a freelancing for it.
When a bug names an issue that tracker has closed, checker reports an outdated tracking for it.
It must be possible for a list to be a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase, without being a rule whose two sides are each one clause.
note: turned the negated bullet into 'without being'
